fi-centropyge-bicolor.title: Bicolor Angelfish
fi-centropyge-bicolor.summary: A dwarf angel, yellow in front and deep blue behind. Not a reliable reef fish.
rows: With caution. Prone to nip stony and soft corals and clam mantles
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae, angelfish foods and mysis or other frozen shrimp
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Samoan and Phoenix Islands, north to southern Japan, south to New Caledonia; throughout Micronesia
notes: Wants lots of rock for grazing and hiding (70 gal or more).

fi-centropyge-bispinosa.title: Coral Beauty Angelfish
fi-centropyge-bispinosa.summary: One of the most popular dwarf angels: deep blue with orange-yellow flanks. Hardy, but may nip corals.
rows: With caution. Prone to nip stony and soft corals
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae, angelfish foods and meaty frozen foods
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Tuamoto Islands, north to the Izu Island, south to Lord Howe Island
notes: Needs a 70 gal or larger tank with rock to graze.

fi-centropyge-eibli.title: Eibl's Angelfish
fi-centropyge-eibli.summary: A dwarf angel from the eastern Indian Ocean, also sold as the Red Stripe Angelfish.
rows: About 6 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 15 cm (5.9 in) TL (FishBase)
With caution. May nip sessile invertebrates and clam mantles
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae and mysis or other frozen shrimp
Eastern Indian Ocean: Sri Lanka to Western Australia, including Indonesia and the Andaman Is
notes: Wants a 70 gal or larger tank with plenty of live rock.

fi-centropyge-vroliki.title: Half Black Angelfish
fi-centropyge-vroliki.summary: A dwarf angel that is pearly in front and black behind.
rows: Keep it as the only dwarf angel in the tank
With caution. May eat soft coral polyps, zoanthids and clam mantles
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae and mysis, plus live rock to graze
Western Pacific: Christmas Island in the eastern Indian Ocean and Bali to the Marshall Islands and Vanuatu, north to southern Japan, south to Lord Howe Island
notes: Wants 70 gal or more with lots of hiding places.

fi-chaetodontoplus-mesoleucus.title: Singapore Angelfish
fi-chaetodontoplus-mesoleucus.summary: A butterflyfish-shaped angel with a black eye mask, white front and dark body. Can be hard to settle in.
rows: About 7 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 18 cm (7.1 in) TL (FishBase)
With caution. Prone to nip stony and soft corals and clam mantles
Omnivore. Grazes microalgae, filamentous algae and diatoms; also offer meaty and angelfish foods
Indo-West Pacific: Japan to Indonesia, Sri Lanka and east to Papua New Guinea
notes: Some refuse food at first; a quiet tank with calm tankmates and hiding places helps.

fi-centropyge-heraldi.title: Herald's Angelfish (Yellow Angel)
rows: With caution. May nip large-polyp stony corals, some soft corals and clam mantles
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae, angelfish foods and meaty items
Indo-Pacific Ocean: from Sri lanka and Bali to the Indo-Malay archipelago to the Marshall Islands
notes: Wants 70 gal or more with plenty of live rock to graze.

fi-centropyge-loricula.title: Flame Angelfish
fi-centropyge-loricula.summary: A popular red-orange dwarf angel. Hardy enough for many tanks, but it may nip corals.
rows: About 4 in (LiveAquaria max size); wild record 15 cm (5.9 in) TL (FishBase)
With caution. Prone to nip stony and soft corals and clam mantles
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae, angelfish foods, mysis or other frozen shrimp and meaty foods
Pacific Ocean: mainly in tropical waters
notes: Needs 70 gal or more with lots of hiding places and live rock to graze.
